newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to inspect proposed N.Korea nuclear site.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to inspect proposed N.Korea nuclear site.

text.p: Taiwan's nuclear watchdog Said on Monday inspectors would go to North Korea in July to examine a proposed site for a controversial dump of Taiwanese nuclear waste.

State-funded radio quoted the Atomic Energy Council as saying that Taiwan Power Co, or Taipower, had proposed a site about 100 km (60 miles) from the border with South Korea, which has launched vehement protests against Taiwan's dumping plan.

"We will go to North Korea for inspection in July, and if North Korea's waste transport or storage does not meet international safety standards, we will not give approval," the radio quoted Chiou Syh-tsong, a council director, as saying.
Taipower's proposed dump would encompass 4.8 sq km (1.85 sq miles) and no one would be allowed to live within a five-km (three-mile) radius, Chiou said.
Taipower in January signed a deal with Pyongyang to store up to 200,000 barrels of low-radiation waste in Stalinist North Korea at a reported price of US$230 million.

South Korea, bitter rival of the North since the Korean War, has strongly opposed the plan, citing possible health hazards and fears of inadequate safety provisions in the North despite Taipower's assurance that the waste was low in radiation.

International environmental group Greenpeace has thrown its support behind South Korea, saying a recent secret inspection of the nuclear dump on Taiwan's outlying Lanyu islet showed the waste was not low in radiation.
Taipower denied the charge, saying it would not have signed the deal to ship the waste if it were not safe.
